sections.title: 1. Understand the design
sections.body:
## One spec, two views

**Native Herdr view** explains the design while your agent stays beside it. **Browser review** keeps decisions, exports and approvals.

Select a scenario below. Diagram and explanation change together.
sections.details:
### Source ownership

Canonical `spec.md` owns requirements. Explanation JSON is a derived teaching artifact, never an approval record.

Agent updates JSON, not executable viewer code. The viewer generates diagrams from bounded nodes and edges.

scenarios.title: Explore a spec
scenarios.body: Agent reads the spec, writes an explanation, then opens this native pane. Select phases and scenarios without leaving Herdr.

diagram.alt: Canonical spec supplies explanation data. Native viewer reads that data and shows the interactive explanation. No decisions are written back.

scenarios.title: Review and approve
scenarios.body: Open the existing HTML review in your browser. Export answers there; agent applies feedback to canonical spec first. Native explanation must be regenerated after material changes.

diagram.alt: Canonical spec generates browser review. Human exports answers. Agent uses those answers to update canonical spec. Native viewer never records approval.

sections.title: 2. Handle failures
sections.body:
## Preserve useful context

Malformed explanation data must not blank the last valid explanation. Diagram generation failure must not hide the text equivalent.
sections.details:
### Deliberate limits

Local files only. No browser embedding, remote resources, shell commands, approval capture or arbitrary executable widgets. Native diagrams use bounded nodes and edges.

scenarios.title: Invalid JSON
scenarios.body: Viewer keeps the last valid explanation and shows an error. Fix JSON; next refresh recovers automatically.

scenarios.title: Missing diagram cache
scenarios.body: Text equivalent stays readable. Use Refresh after fixing app-data write permissions.
